issues.claim: price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: "plus $0-$60/year for software or monitoring" while the same band lists "SimpliSafe Water Sensor $19.99 with plans from 33 cents/day self monitoring to 76 cents/day Standard"
issues.problem: The stated annual band does not follow from the figures cited inside it. 33 cents/day is about $120/year and 76 cents/day is about $277/year, both far above the $60/year ceiling, and SimpliSafe's plan page shows those per-day prices. The band and its own evidence disagree in the range the brief uses to describe the low end of the market.
issues.fix: Split the low-cost band: one-time hardware $19.99-$105 per sensor (or $579.99 for a whole-home shutoff device); software $0-$60/year (Monnit Basic free, iMonnit Premiere from $45/yr, FireAvert PRO $60/yr); residential monitored plans stated separately at 33 cents-$2.66/day (roughly $120-$971/year), billed per household system rather than per sensor and therefore not comparable with the annual software figures.

issues.claim: SimpliSafe Water Sensor "$19.99 one-time" and "works with the base station; alerts whether armed or not", sourced to https://support.simplisafe.com/pages/monitoring-plans
issues.problem: The cited page is the plan comparison table only (33 cents, 76 cents, $1.10, $1.66-$2.66 per day) and says nothing about the sensor. On the live simplisafe.com water-sensor page no price is rendered, and simplisafe.com/alarm-sensors also returns the sensor description with no readable price; the $19.99 appears only in a search rendering of simplisafe.com/alarm-sensors. The always-armed/base-station wording comes from a separate support article. Unlike Moen and Phyn, this script-rendered figure is not flagged in the caveats.
issues.fix: Flag the $19.99 the same way Moen and Phyn are flagged (search-rendered, not readable on the live page, re-check before quoting), and cite simplisafe.com/alarm-sensors plus support.simplisafe.com/articles/water-sensor/water-sensor-installation-guide for the price and the inclusion.

issues.claim: YoLink offerings: Water Leak Sensor 4 "$19.99 each" and Hub "$23.59 each (sale price; list price shown as $29.99)", both sourced to the Water Leak Sensor 1 Starter Kit URL
issues.problem: Citation mismatch. The cited starter-kit page shows only $58.99 / $75.98 and Sensor 1 copy; it carries no Sensor 4 or hub price. Both figures are correct, but only on the individual product pages (shop.yosmart.com/products/ys7906 shows $19.99; shop.yosmart.com/products/ys1603 shows $23.59 struck from $29.99).
issues.fix: Add the two product URLs to the YoLink entry (or give each tier its own source URL), keeping the starter-kit URL only for the kit price.

issues.claim: YoLink starter kit "includes: One hub plus four Water Leak Sensor 1 units" (repeated in caveats)
issues.problem: Not stated on the cited page. The kit page's meta description says "Detect water at the selected number of locations", implying a selectable pack size, and the visible copy mentions Sensor 1 electrodes plus a SpeakerHub with no sensor count. A third-party retail listing describes a "Water Sensor 4-Pack Hub Kit", consistent with four but not the vendor page. The caveat that the kit price and the $19.99 Sensor 4 price are not interchangeable depends on this composition.
issues.fix: Describe the kit as "hub plus Water Leak Sensor 1 sensors, quantity set by the pack-size selector, $58.99 (list $75.98)" unless a page showing exactly four sensors can be cited, and soften the caveat to match.

issues.claim: Phyn "includes" list (pre-freeze warnings, Plumbing Check, SMS/push alerts from a free app, multi-property up to 6, unions and adapters not included) and "installation typically one to two hours per the page", sourced to https://thehomebriefing.com/products/phyn-phyn-plus-2nd-gen/
issues.problem: The cited third-party profile is a short specification record: it confirms the $579.99 manufacturer-listed direct price, pressure-wave analysis, auto/remote shutoff, a 12-foot power requirement and that adapters are not included, but not the free app, pre-freeze warnings, Plumbing Check, six-property limit, SMS/push alerts, Alexa/Google/IFTTT or the one-to-two-hour install. All of those are on phyn.com, so the facts hold but the citation is wrong for them.
issues.fix: Keep thehomebriefing for the $579.99 only, and cite https://phyn.com/products/phyn-plus-smart-water-assistant-shutoff-v2 (which also states unions and adapters are sold separately and shows no readable price) for the inclusions and install time.

issues.problem: Inconsistent with the brief's own low-cost band of "$19.99-$105 one-time per sensor, or $579.99 for a whole-home shutoff device". Monnit's $105 sensor and the $579.99 Phyn device are both self-serve purchases, so the $40 ceiling is not the band the brief sources.
issues.fix: Change the summary to "$19.99-$105 self-serve sensors, or $579.99 for a whole-home shutoff device" so it matches the low-cost band.

issues.claim: Parker Plumbing Critical Facility tier: "Buildings with more systems to watch; same inclusions"
issues.problem: Incomplete against the page, which describes Critical Facility as 15+ monitoring points and adds "Cellular and BAS connections where specified" to the shared inclusion list. That difference matters to the integration comparison the brief draws.
issues.fix: Change to "15+ monitoring points; same inclusions plus cellular and BAS connections where specified".

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs: "A 161-unit property paying about $1,063/month ... roughly $6.60 per unit per month"
issues.problem: The $1,063 and the 161 units are stated on the page; the ~$6.60 per unit is arithmetic the page does not state and is not labelled as inference, unlike the brief's other derived figures.
issues.fix: Keep $1,063/month and 161 units as sourced facts and mark the ~$6.60/unit as arithmetic (1,063 / 161), or drop it.

issues.claim: YoLink contract_terms: "No contract, no subscription for basic app alerts; 60-day returns from delivery, customer-paid return shipping"
issues.problem: The 60-day return and customer-paid return shipping are on the page and confirmed, but the page says nothing about contracts or subscriptions, so the first half is unsourced from this vendor page.
issues.fix: Keep the returns terms and either cite a YoLink page stating no subscription is needed for app alerts, or mark that half as unstated.

issues.claim: Moen Leak Protection Service "$17.99/month plus $49.99 activation fee"
issues.problem: Not a failure, but recorded for the record: the flo.moen.com product page body, fetched twice, contains the 36-month term, 50% cancellation fee, month-to-month renewal, independent-installer and warranty terms but no dollar figures. The figures reappear only in a search rendering of the same Moen product URL and match $17.99/month and $49.99 activation. The brief discloses this and uses no Moen number in the ranges, which is acceptable.
issues.fix: No change needed beyond keeping the disclosure; do not move the Moen figures into any computed range until a readable price is captured.
